brief.headline: Aluminium reclaimed the level it lost the day before and led a rising base-metals board - but it did all of that in the hours BEFORE the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023, so the price on this page has not yet been tested by the news.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: on the 16-September LME official, aluminium cash settled $3,310.00, up $50.00 or +1.53%, and three-month $3,289.00, up $53.00 or +1.64% - the strongest single session of this fifteen-session window. Both legs reclaimed the 3,261 level that both had lost the day before. Every other base metal rose or held: copper +1.10%, zinc +1.13%, lead +0.75%, nickel unchanged.

THE TIMING IS THE STORY: the LME official is struck at 13:20 London and the Federal Reserve announced at 19:00 London the same day. The Committee raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, unanimously, the first increase since 2023, with 16 of 18 participants projecting at least one more. NONE OF THAT IS IN THE PRICES ON THIS PAGE. What is visible is the reaction in markets that kept trading: the dollar index firmed to about 100.3, the US ten-year yield went to roughly 5.02% and is described as a nineteen-year high, equities fell sharply and Brent dropped about 2.9% to roughly $105.60.

WHAT DID NOT CONFIRM: the backwardation narrowed from $24.00 to $21.00 even as the flat price rose 1.5% - the spread and the price moved in opposite directions - and warehouse stock was UNCHANGED at 243,600 tonnes, the first session in this window with no draw. So the rally came without either of the two physical corroborations that were available. A curve that flattens into a rising price is more consistent with forward buying than with prompt scarcity.

WHAT TO WATCH: today's 13:20 London official is the first exchange settlement that actually contains the Fed decision, and a stronger dollar mechanically raises the price of a dollar metal in every other currency. On the supply side, a major Gulf producer publicly stated on 16-September that it has restored output to about 80% of pre-war levels and is exporting through Red Sea and Omani ports - the clearest evidence yet that the Gulf disruption is unwinding, which is the largest bearish supply development available to this market.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: THE MARKET TOOK BACK TUESDAY'S FALL AND THEN SOME, AND IT DID SO BEFORE THE FEDERAL RESERVE SPOKE. Anyone reading this board as the market's verdict on the Fed is reading it wrong; today's 13:20 official is the first exchange settlement that actually contains the decision. THE SPREAD DID NOT CONFIRM THE RALLY, AND THAT IS THE SECOND THING WORTH RECORDING. Cash rose $50.00 while three-month rose $53.00, so the cash-to-three-month BACKWARDATION NARROWED from $24.00 to $21.00. The price and the spread therefore moved in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS on this session - a rising flat price alongside a flattening front - which is the mirror image of Monday, when both widened together. THREE SESSIONS HAVE NOW PRODUCED A WIDENING, A HALVING AND A FURTHER NARROWING WHILE THE FLAT PRICE WENT UP, DOWN AND UP: the spread is not currently tracking the price in any stable way and should not be used as a directional signal on one session. THE STOCK LINE STOPPED FALLING FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS WINDOW: warehouse stock was UNCHANGED at 243,600 tonnes, a zero change against draws on every prior session of the fifteen-session window. That is a break in the one series that had been consistent, and it is recorded rather than smoothed over. THE CROSS-METAL PICTURE WAS BROADLY POSITIVE: copper three-month rose 1.10%, zinc 1.13%, lead 0.75%, aluminium 1.64% and nickel was unchanged, so aluminium led a board that rose together rather than outperforming a weak one.

kpis.label: LME warehouse stock (t)
kpis.note: LME ALUMINIUM WAREHOUSE STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 243,600 TONNES ON 16-SEPTEMBER, A ZERO CHANGE REPORTED EXPLICITLY AS ZERO ON BOTH WESTMETALL LANGUAGE OVERVIEWS. THIS IS THE FIRST SESSION IN THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW ON WHICH STOCK DID NOT FALL, and the break matters because the drawdown was the one series that had been running in a straight line while the price and the spread oscillated. Over the window stock has fallen from 246,825 tonnes on 26-August to 243,600 - a draw of 3,225 tonnes, or 1.3%, in fifteen sessions. Publicly reported context describes LME aluminium inventories as close to a 36-year low with SHFE stockpiles also falling. ONE FLAT SESSION IS NOT A TREND CHANGE AND IS NOT PRESENTED AS ONE; it is the absence of the day's confirmation rather than a contradiction. What it does remove is the ability to say that the physical market drew metal on the same day the price rose, which would have been the cleanest bullish combination available.

kpis.label: Cash-to-3M spread ($/t)
kpis.note: THE CURVE REMAINS IN BACKWARDATION - CASH $3,310.00 ABOVE THREE-MONTH $3,289.00 BY $21.00 - BUT THE BACKWARDATION NARROWED AGAIN, FROM $24.00, AND IT NARROWED ON A DAY THE FLAT PRICE ROSE 1.5%. THE SPREAD AND THE PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THAT IS CALLED OUT EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE READER TO NOTICE. Convention on this page: cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION and indicates prompt tightness; cash below three-month is CONTANGO. $21.00 IS THE NARROWEST BACKWARDATION OF THE LAST FIVE SESSIONS and roughly 0.6% of the flat price - present but shallow. THE THREE-SESSION SEQUENCE IS $24.00, $54.00, $24.00, $21.00 ACROSS 11, 14, 15 AND 16 SEPTEMBER. A spread that doubles, halves and then edges lower again around an unchanged market structure is behaving like a prompt-date artefact, not like a tightening trend, and this page has now said so on three consecutive runs rather than re-interpreting it each morning. THE COMPARISON WITH THE PEER BOARD IS THE USEFUL PART: aluminium and zinc are backwardated on this session while copper, nickel and lead are all in contango, so aluminium's prompt remains structurally firmer than most of the board even as the degree of that firmness erodes.

lme.commentary: A NEW OFFICIAL PUBLISHED AND IT WAS THE STRONGEST SESSION OF THIS WINDOW - BUT IT WAS STRUCK BEFORE THE NEWS THAT MATTERED. On 16-September LME aluminium cash settled $3,310.00 against $3,260.00, UP $50.00 or +1.53%; three-month settled $3,289.00 against $3,236.00, UP $53.00 or +1.64%; warehouse stock was UNCHANGED at 243,600 tonnes; and the cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed from $24.00 to $21.00. THE LME OFFICIAL IS STRUCK AT 13:20 LONDON AND THE FEDERAL RESERVE ANNOUNCED AT 19:00 LONDON ON THE SAME DAY, so this entire board predates a 25-basis-point increase to 3.75-4.00% - the first since 2023 - and predates the dollar, yield and equity moves that followed it. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE PAGE AND IT IS PUT FIRST RATHER THAN IN A FOOTNOTE. THREE THINGS ARE WORTH SEPARATING. FIRST, THE TECHNICAL EVENT IS REAL AND WAS PRE-ANNOUNCED HERE: both legs of the curve reclaimed 3,261, the level both lost the day before, with three-month $28.00 above it and cash $49.00 above it. Yesterday this page named that reclaim as the specific test into this session; it was met, and the daily count is upgraded accordingly. SECOND, THE PHYSICAL CONFIRMATION DID NOT ARRIVE. Stock was flat for the first time in fifteen sessions - not a build, but not the draw that would have paired with a rising price - and the backwardation narrowed while the flat price rose, so the spread and the price moved in OPPOSITE directions. A curve that flattens into a rally is more consistent with forward buying than with prompt scarcity, and the three-month rising more than cash says the same thing. THIRD, THE BREADTH WAS GOOD BUT NOT DISTINGUISHING: copper +1.10%, zinc +1.13%, lead +0.75%, nickel unchanged. Aluminium led, but it led a board that rose together, which is a weaker relative signal than outperforming a falling one. THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT ALUMINIUM WON A TECHNICAL ARGUMENT IN THE MORNING AND WAS THEN HANDED A HARDER MACRO ENVIRONMENT IN THE EVENING, AND TODAY'S 13:20 RING IS THE FIRST PLACE THOSE TWO FACTS MEET.

drivers.text: THE TARIFF LEG ROSE $25.00 TODAY WITH NO POLICY CHANGE AT ALL — Section 232 on aluminium articles is an AD-VALOREM duty levied on value, verified again this run at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives under the proclamation signed 01-June-2026 and effective 08-June-2026 through 31-December-2027, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. Applied to the 16-September cash settlement of $3,310.00 the tariff leg alone is $1,655.00, against $1,630.00 on Tuesday's $3,260.00 cash. IT ROSE BECAUSE THE METAL PRICE ROSE, NOT BECAUSE ANYTHING IN WASHINGTON CHANGED - the exact mirror of yesterday's $25.50 fall. Against the carried duty-paid level of about $2,403/t, the implied market leg is roughly $748.00, or about 31% of the delivered premium, down from about 32% yesterday, again purely as an arithmetic consequence of a higher metal price. This decomposition is recomputed every run and is arithmetic, not an assessment.
drivers.source: US Section 232 adjustment - 50% on aluminium articles, 25% on derivatives, effective 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027

drivers.text: A CANADA-ONLY TARIFF CUT WOULD NOT FIX THE US PREMIUM, ON THE RECORD — Alcoa's chief financial officer stated publicly at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference on 14-September that the US Midwest premium currently stands at about $1.09 per pound, roughly $2,403 per tonne, down from a June record of $1.19 per pound, and that removing the tariff on Canadian metal alone would not bring it down significantly. The stated arithmetic is the reason: the United States must import about 4 Mt/y of primary aluminium against roughly 3 Mt of Canadian capability, so a unilateral Canadian exemption leaves about a quarter of import demand still paying the full duty and the marginal tonne still sets the premium. THIS IS A NAMED PRODUCER PUTTING NUMBERS ON A STRUCTURAL CLAIM AND IT REMAINS THE STRONGEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE ON THIS PANEL.
drivers.source: AL Circle, 14-September-2026 - Alcoa says Canada tariff cut alone won't bring US aluminium premium down

drivers.text: RETURNING GULF SUPPLY IS THE NEW BEARISH FORCE ON ASIAN AND EUROPEAN PREMIUMS — Aluminium Bahrain's chief executive told Reuters on 16-September, on the sidelines of the Fastmarkets aluminium conference in Budapest, that the company is producing at around 80% of pre-Iran-war levels and is exporting metal through the Saudi Red Sea port of Jeddah and from Sohar in Oman. Alba had shut reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted supply chains, and its plant was struck in late March; the damage was described as repaired and covered by insurance. THE PREMIUM RELEVANCE IS DIRECT AND IT IS TWO-SIDED. Asian and European premiums spiked on the loss of Gulf tonnes and on the freight and war-risk cost of moving what remained; a producer back to four-fifths of pre-war output that has ALSO SOLVED ITS ROUTING by shipping through Red Sea and Omani ports removes both legs of that argument at once. THIS IS ONE COMPANY'S DATED PUBLIC STATEMENT, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND NO PREMIUM ROW HAS BEEN MOVED ON IT.
drivers.source: SMM / Reuters, 16-September-2026 - Alba restores 80% of pre-war aluminium production, exports via Saudi and Oman ports

drivers.text: A STRONGER DOLLAR RAISES THE LOCAL COST OF THE SAME TONNE EVERYWHERE OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES — The Federal Reserve raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, the first increase since 2023, and the dollar index rose about 0.62% to roughly 100.33 with EUR/USD down about 0.61% to roughly 1.14646. PREMIUMS ARE QUOTED IN DOLLARS BUT PAID OUT OF LOCAL REVENUE, so a stronger dollar raises the all-in local cost of imported metal without any premium assessment changing. For a European buyer the three-month alone moved from about EUR 2,806 to about EUR 2,869 a tonne overnight. THIS IS AN ARITHMETIC OBSERVATION ABOUT CURRENCY, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT PREMIUM DIRECTION, and no row has been moved on it.

A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

status.status: MATERIAL RESTART CONFIRMED ON THE RECORD - PRODUCING AT ABOUT 80% OF PRE-IRAN-WAR LEVELS AND EXPORTING VIA JEDDAH (RED SEA) AND SOHAR (OMAN)
status.update: THE SINGLE LARGEST CHANGE ON THIS PANEL THIS RUN. Alba's chief executive Ali Al Baqali told Reuters on 16-September, on the sidelines of the Fastmarkets aluminium conference in Budapest, that the company is producing at around 80% of pre-Iran-war levels. Alba had shut reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 after the outbreak of the war when the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted supply chains, and the plant was hit by an Iranian strike in late March which the chief executive described as a small, minor attack; he said the damage was repaired and covered by insurance. THE ROUTING DETAIL MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE OUTPUT NUMBER: exporting through the Saudi Red Sea port of Jeddah and from Sohar in Oman demonstrates a working commercial route that does not depend on the Strait reopening. Alba describes itself as the world's biggest aluminium smelter on one site, with capacity of about 1,623 kt. THIS PAGE PREVIOUSLY CARRIED THIS ROW AS LINES 1, 2 AND 3 IDLED SINCE MARCH WITH NO DATED RESTART SCHEDULE; that framing is now superseded by a dated statement from the company and the change is recorded rather than quietly swapped in. trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN CHURNED DAILY, AND THIS RUN IS A MATERIAL-CHANGE REVIEW RATHER THAN A CALENDAR ONE. TWO THINGS TRIGGERED IT. SECOND, THE ALUMINA CORRIDOR: dated 12-September evidence shows Asia exporting 7.05 Mt of alumina in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year, with India swinging to a 1.72 Mt trade surplus on exports up 51.3% and imports down 34.9%. flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.

flows.note: REVISED THIS RUN AND THE REVISION IS EXPLAINED. Dated reporting of 07-September-2026 has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes, the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate 26-August report states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no agreement is signed. THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS EVIDENTIAL CATEGORY, FROM UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR TO DATED MULTI-OUTLET REPORTING, AND THAT IS WHY THE CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED WHILE THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS NOT DECLARED REPAIRED. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

FROM 08-SEPTEMBER CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFF ON US STEEL AND ALUMINIUM RISES FROM 25% TO 50%, matched to the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars. catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON, AND IT IS THE FIRST EXCHANGE SETTLEMENT THAT ACTUALLY CONTAINS THE FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION. Everything on this page's board was struck before the announcement. THE SPECIFIC QUESTION IS WHETHER THE THREE-MONTH HOLDS THE 3,261 LEVEL IT RECLAIMED YESTERDAY with a dollar index above 100 and a nineteen-year-high ten-year yield behind it. Holding it through a hawkish surprise would be a far stronger signal than yesterday's reclaim; giving it straight back would say the reclaim was a pre-decision position adjustment. Watch the stock line too - a second consecutive flat or building session would break the drawdown trend outright.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE OPENS TODAY. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch marks settle on a monthly cycle around the 17th-18th, so the next opportunity for a new public mark on those rows is today or tomorrow. Together those two lines are roughly 15-19% of smelter cash cost. THE DIRECTIONAL INPUT REVERSED OVERNIGHT: Brent fell about 2.2% to roughly $105.60 after the Fed decision, against the four-month high this page recorded yesterday, which argues for a softer rather than a firmer settlement. The SMM fluoride-salt weekly cycle that sets the AlF3 and cryolite rows also falls on 18-September.

THE 40TH FASTMARKETS INTERNATIONAL ALUMINIUM CONFERENCE CONCLUDES IN BUDAPEST TODAY, having already produced the most consequential disclosure of this run - Alba's statement to Reuters that it is at about 80% of pre-war output and exporting through Jeddah and Sohar. Conference weeks are when producers, traders and price-reporting agencies make the public statements that subsequently move assessed premiums, and this one overlaps live Q4 Japanese quarterly negotiations. This page will treat anything said there as evidence only when it is reported with a date and a source.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE: a US vehicle and dairy import ban follows the 50% tariff on about 100 categories of Canadian products that took effect on 15-September. Canada's 50% counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports. The read-through to primary aluminium is indirect but automotive is a top-two end-use for North American rolled and extruded metal, and dated reporting already records auto-parts supply chains under pressure.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT. Q3 settled at a record $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July; producer offers for October-December shipments have been reported at $310-325/t, 18-22% below, and a consensus range of $280-310/t has been reported. Dated September reporting describes spot indications subdued around $320-380/t with buyers resisting. ALBA'S CONFIRMED RETURN TO ABOUT 80% OF PRE-WAR OUTPUT IS A NEW AND DIRECTLY RELEVANT SUPPLY FACT that leans on the lower half of that range. A settlement near $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% from the Q3 record in a single quarter and would be the largest single premium event of the year in Asia.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND IT NOW MATTERS MORE THAN IT DID. With 16 of 18 participants projecting at least one further increase this year and four seeing two, the market's question has moved from whether the Fed would start to how far it goes. Each further increase is another turn of the same three screws on this market: a stronger dollar, a higher carry cost on physical metal, and a higher discount rate on the restart and expansion pipeline listed on this page.

risks.text: THE FEDERAL RESERVE HAS MOVED FROM EVENT RISK TO STANDING HEADWIND, AND THAT IS A WORSE STATE FOR THIS MARKET THAN THE ONE IT REPLACED. RAISED TO UP AND RE-FRAMED THIS RUN. The Committee raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously 12-0, the first increase since 2023, and the projections showed 16 of 18 participants expecting at least one further increase this year with four seeing two. The dollar index broke 100 to about 100.33, EUR/USD fell to about 1.14646, the ten-year rose to about 5.023% and is described as a nineteen-year high, and US equities fell sharply. FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED INDUSTRIAL METAL THIS IS THREE SEPARATE CHANNELS AT ONCE: a stronger dollar raises the local cost of the same tonne everywhere outside the United States, a higher long yield raises the carry cost of holding physical metal, and a higher discount rate lowers the present value of every restart and expansion project. THE 16-SEPTEMBER LME BOARD ON THIS PAGE PREDATES ALL OF IT.

THE GULF SUPPLY OUTAGE HAS STARTED TO UNWIND ON THE RECORD, AND IT IS THE LARGEST BEARISH SUPPLY DEVELOPMENT AVAILABLE TO THIS MARKET. MOVED FROM FLAT TO UP THIS RUN ON A DATED NAMED-COMPANY STATEMENT. Aluminium Bahrain's chief executive told Reuters on 16-September that the company is producing at about 80% of pre-Iran-war levels and is exporting through the Saudi Red Sea port of Jeddah and from Sohar in Oman; the late-March strike damage was described as repaired and insured. ALBA HAD LINES 1, 2 AND 3 IDLED - ROUGHLY 311,000 TONNES ANNUALISED OF A 1,623 kt PLANT - AND THIS PAGE CARRIED THAT AS AN OPEN-ENDED OUTAGE AS RECENTLY AS YESTERDAY. THE ROUTING DETAIL IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF: shipping through Red Sea and Omani ports demonstrates that Gulf metal can reach buyers WITHOUT the Strait of Hormuz reopening, which removes the freight-and-access argument that has underpinned Asian and European premiums. The rest of the Gulf is unchanged - EGA at 315 of 1,262 reduction cells with full production targeted for Q1-2027, Qatalum at about 60% of a 648 kt nameplate with no dated restart - so this is one producer, not the region. NO TONNAGE OR DATED RAMP SCHEDULE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED AND NONE IS ASSUMED.

TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, REMAINS THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE, AND THE NEXT DATED STEP IS 29-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. Section 232 was re-verified this run at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives under the proclamation signed 01-June-2026 and effective 08-June-2026 through 31-December-2027, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. The US 50% tariff on about 100 categories of Canadian products took effect on 15-September and a vehicle and dairy import ban follows on 29-September; Canada's 50% counter-tariffs have been in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports. A named producer stated on 14-September that a Canada-only cut would NOT bring the Midwest premium down significantly, because the US must import about 4 Mt/y against roughly 3 Mt of Canadian capability. THE RISK IS ESCALATING ON A PUBLISHED SCHEDULE, WHICH IS WHY THE TREND STAYS UP.

THE COST FLOOR UNDER THE MARKET IS FALLING ON EVERY LINE AT ONCE, WHICH LOWERS THE PRICE AT WHICH MARGINAL SUPPLY IS FORCED OUT. HELD AT DOWN because the risk of a cost-driven price floor is receding rather than building. A dated 17-September SMM alumina morning comment records the SMM alumina index at 2,674.36 yuan/mt, FOB Western Australia FLAT at $349/mt, the ex-China premium steady at 312 yuan/mt and Chinese weekly alumina output still RISING as a Shanxi refinery fully restores. On the energy side European gas fell 4.72% to about EUR 77.75/MWh and Brent fell about 2.2% to roughly $105.60 - power is 30-40% of cash cost and the carbon rows a further 15-19%. PUBLISHED ANALYSIS DESCRIBES A SUSTAINED ALUMINA SURPLUS OF 0.8-1.1 Mt with substantial capacity additions across China, India, Indonesia and Guinea. CHEAPER INPUTS ARE MARGIN TODAY AND SUPPLY TOMORROW: Press Metal's Q2 result, added to the history panel this run, names lower alumina cost as a driver of a 78.9% rise in pre-tax profit - the mechanism is now visible in a reported P&L, not just in a model.

THE FRONT OF THE CURVE IS A NOISY INDICATOR AND SHOULD NOT BE TRADED AS A TREND SIGNAL ON ONE SESSION. HELD AT UP. The cash-to-three-month backwardation has gone $24.00, $54.00, $24.00, $21.00 across 11, 14, 15 and 16 September around an unchanged market structure. ON 16-SEPTEMBER IT NARROWED WHILE THE FLAT PRICE ROSE 1.53% - the spread and the price moving in OPPOSITE directions - and the three-month rose more than cash, which is the signature of forward buying rather than prompt scarcity. THE RISK IS NOT THAT THE MARKET IS LOOSE: it has been backwardated on every session of this window and aluminium is one of only two metals on the board with a backwardation at all. THE RISK IS THAT ANYONE READING A SINGLE SESSION'S SPREAD AS EVIDENCE OF PHYSICAL TIGHTENING HAS NOW BEEN WRONG THREE TIMES IN FOUR SESSIONS.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN - THE MOST CONSISTENT BULLISH SERIES ON THIS PAGE - PAUSED FOR THE FIRST TIME. NEW THIS RUN AND SET AT UP. LME aluminium warehouse stock was UNCHANGED at 243,600 tonnes on 16-September, a reported zero change, after falling on every other session of the fifteen-session window. Over the window stock has still drawn 3,225 tonnes, or 1.3%, and publicly reported context puts LME inventories close to a 36-year low, so the level remains supportive. ONE FLAT SESSION IS NOT A TREND CHANGE AND IS NOT PRESENTED AS ONE. THE RISK IS SPECIFIC AND NARROW: the draw was the one series that had not oscillated, and a market whose bullish case leans on falling visible inventory needs that series to keep falling. Elsewhere on the same board copper built 4,925 tonnes, zinc 1,450 and nickel 210, so the peer group is accumulating metal while aluminium merely stopped losing it.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS VISIBLE, DATED AND SLOW, AND IT CAPS THE UPSIDE OVER YEARS RATHER THAN WEEKS. HELD AT FLAT. The publicly reported pipeline includes Alcoa's San Ciprian ramp toward full capacity at 228,000 t/y, Slovalco's first 75,000 t/y of a 175,000 t total with production expected to resume in Q4-2026 under a Slovak government carbon-compensation package, Magnitude 7's first potline of about 75,000 t/y before the end of 2026, Century's Mt Holly back at full capacity, and EGA's phased Al Taweelah return targeted for Q1-2027. THE ECONOMICS OF EVERY ONE OF THOSE IMPROVED ON 16-SEPTEMBER: European gas fell 4.72%, which is the single variable Slovalco's restart economics turn on. Commodity-board commentary explicitly names restarts, expansions and rising Chinese exports as factors that could ease constraints and limit price gains. NONE OF IT IS FAST AND NONE OF IT IS SPECULATIVE, WHICH IS WHY THE TREND IS FLAT RATHER THAN UP.

A PREMIUM PANEL WHERE EVERY ROW IS STALE IS A DATA RISK IN ITS OWN RIGHT, AND IT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. HELD AT FLAT. No newer dated public assessment printed for ANY premium region into this window, so the Asian, European and US rows are all carried at their last dated marks, with the Platts Midwest transaction row dated 20-August sitting more than $300/t below a 14-September producer disclosure on a different basis. THE Q4 JAPANESE QUARTERLY IS UNDER NEGOTIATION 18-28% BELOW A RECORD Q3 AND WILL SETTLE IN THE COMING WEEKS; the range on this page remains $280-310 and has deliberately NOT been narrowed for a third consecutive run. Alba's restart statement leans on the lower half of that range but is not a settlement and has not been used to move it. Anyone using these rows should read the dates before the levels.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

caveats: THE BOARD ON THIS PAGE IS THE COMPLETE 16-SEPTEMBER LME OFFICIAL, NOT A LIVE PRICE. This page compiles at about 06:10 London on Thursday 17-September and today's official prints at 13:20. The entire exchange board - cash, three-month, stocks and FX - belongs to the PRIOR session, and nothing intraday has been invented.

THE 16-SEPTEMBER BOARD PREDATES THE FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION BY NEARLY SIX HOURS AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE PAGE. The LME official is struck at 13:20 London; the FOMC announced at 19:00 London the same day. No exchange price shown here prices the 25-basis-point increase to 3.75-4.00%. The macro panel, which is read off a continuously traded reference board this morning, DOES contain it. The two panels are therefore measuring different moments and that is stated rather than reconciled into a single view.

THE SESSION WAS VERIFIED FOR COMPLETENESS, NOT JUST FOR DATE. Both Westmetall language overviews were re-requested cache-busted this morning and agree line for line on 16-September across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings, and every per-metal daily table shows no row after 16-September. The known failure mode on this source is a stale cached snapshot in either language, and it has been checked for in both directions.

THE ALUMINIUM STOCK FIGURE OF 243,600 TONNES IS AN UNCHANGED READING, REPORTED AS A ZERO CHANGE ON BOTH LANGUAGE OVERVIEWS. It is a genuine flat session and not a carried-forward or missing value; a zero is shown as a zero.

THE MACRO PANEL IS A COMMODITY AND CURRENCY REFERENCE BOARD, NOT A SET OF EXCHANGE SETTLEMENTS, AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH ON EVERY ROW. Day-changes on that panel are computed against the level THIS PAGE CARRIED YESTERDAY from the same board rather than against the board's own day-change field, whose sign convention is not reliably disclosed.

EVERY PREMIUM ROW IS CARRIED AT A LAST DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT AND NONE WAS REFRESHED THIS RUN. Premium assessments are periodic; a row that has not changed has no newer public evidence behind it, not an oversight. The Platts MW US Transaction row is dated 20-August and sits more than $300/t below a 14-September producer disclosure on a different basis; the two have deliberately NOT been reconciled into one number. Read the dates before the levels.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY RANGE OF $280-310/t WAS NOT NARROWED THIS RUN, FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE RUN. A range is not tightened on repeated readings of the same source. Alba's restart statement is a directional argument for the lower half of it, not a settlement, and has not been used to move it.

THE ALBA RESTART IS ONE NAMED COMPANY'S DATED PUBLIC STATEMENT TO A NEWS AGENCY, NOT A REGULATORY DISCLOSURE AND NOT A TONNAGE SCHEDULE. No precise volume, no dated ramp plan and no guidance revision has been published, and none has been assumed. The rest of the Gulf - EGA and Qatalum - is unchanged on this page.

THE INPUT BASKET ROWS OTHER THAN COPPER ARE CARRIED AT PERIODIC MARKS AND THEIR STALENESS IS DECLARED ON EACH ROW. The monthly carbon settlement window for prebaked anodes and coal tar pitch opens today and has not printed; nothing has been appended to those histories and no value has been inferred from the fall in Brent. Rows with no public series at all - electricity, cathode blocks, titanium-boron grain refiner - carry an empty history and say why.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE PANEL IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, AND NOT A FORECAST OF FACT. Historical pivots are locked; only confirmed settlements are added; probabilities are the author's and are stated so they can be disagreed with. The invalidation levels are published precisely so the count can be shown to be wrong.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC INFORMATION FROM A CITED SOURCE. No confidential, internal, company-specific commercial information appears anywhere on this page: no realised prices, net-backs, volumes, costs, shipping lanes or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is publicly disclosed listed-company information in the peer-earnings and producer-status panels.
